after: Persistent observance can be heard as one manner of devotion toward the deity named by Allah.
reason: In this branch, حَٰفِظَٰتٌ means persevering in a matter; ٱللَّهُ names the one worshipped, so constancy shades the worship relation.

after: Keeping to a good course helps preserve its soundness over time.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ carries the sense of continuing steadily, while فَٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ names soundness and rectitude; sustained practice supports that quality.

after: Guarding is heard as a steady practice rather than a single act. قَٰنِتَٰتٌ gives that constancy its devotional form as obedient adherence.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ in this branch means persevering in a matter, while قَٰنِتَٰتٌ means religious obedience; each names ongoing fidelity from a different side.

after: The sense of constancy can lightly color devotion directed toward Allah.
reason: The rare sense of حَٰفِظَٰتٌ is habitual persistence, and ٱللَّهُ is the worshipped being; their link is a generic one of sustained worship.

after: Steady attention can be faintly set against the resting posture of a bed.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ here means keeping at a matter, whereas ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ are places where the side lies down; diligence and rest offer a thin contrast.

after: The keeping sense of حَٰفِظَٰتٌ makes compliance sound like continued adherence. The women’s response is thus heard as steadfast following, not a passing concession.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ means persevering in a matter; أَطَعْنَكُمْ means complying and following readily, so both express adherence sustained in action.

after: Guarding as steady observance brings a faint echo of devotion to Allah.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ has the rare sense of keeping faithfully at something, while ٱللَّهَ is the worshipped one; the relation is the general one between constancy and worship.

after: The warning can awaken the attentive state described by the rare branch.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ here is vigilance and little heedlessness; فَعِظُوهُنَّ is a heart-softening admonition, which can prompt that watchfulness.

after: Vigilance stands sharply beside the beds and lying-down places. The contrast makes the bed’s restfulness more audible against the women’s watchful care.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ in this branch means alertness and freedom from heedlessness; ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ names places of lying down, an image of rest set against vigilance.

after: Protective zeal can be heard as one motive for the men’s role of care.
reason: The branch of حَٰفِظَٰتٌ means anger and protective honor, while قَوَّٰمُونَ names the men as a group; the connection between group responsibility and protective feeling is broad.

after: The rising or protruding image may faintly picture a body bristling in protective anger.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ carries the rare sense of indignation and zeal; نُشُوزَهُنَّ in the supplied plain sense is a rise or protrusion, making only a thin bodily image.

after: Protective anger may be redirected into the measured speech of admonition.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ here evokes anger on behalf of honor, whereas فَعِظُوهُنَّ is a reminder that softens the heart; counsel can give that force a gentler form.

after: The sense of defending a trust can sit alongside the men-class named in the opening claim.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ in this branch means protecting inviolabilities and covenants; قَوَّٰمُونَ here is glossed as a group of men, so the link is a general role pairing.

after: Guardianship becomes most vivid precisely when the protected person is absent. The unseen is not an empty space but the condition in which fidelity is kept.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ carries the sense of preserving a covenant during someone’s absence; لِّلْغَيْبِ names absence and what is unseen, completing the domain of that keeping.

after: The command to strike is heard beside a word for defending what must remain inviolable. That pairing makes the force of the blow answer to the demand for protection.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ here evokes defending sanctities and preventing violation; وَٱضْرِبُوهُنَّ in its plain sense is to strike, placing protection beside bodily impact.

after: The keeping of what is sacred can be heard beside the divine predicate of exaltedness.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ means protecting inviolabilities and covenants, while عَلِيًّا means high or exalted; the connection is the broad one between safeguarding what is honored and its high rank.

after: Admonition can serve as a step toward the clear course evoked by the rare path sense.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ here carries the image of a straight, unbroken path; فَعِظُوهُنَّ is a warning reminder, which may guide someone back toward such a course.

after: The rare path sense is directly echoed by the closing word for a way. A clear, unbroken course is heard inside the prohibition against seeking any avenue against them.
reason: حَٰفِظَٰتٌ in this branch evokes a straight path that does not break; سَبِيلًا is a path or way, so the two words meet in the same road image.

after: The beds become hollows into which bodies settle and partly disappear from view. That low, concealing image gives the lying places a hidden depth.
reason: لِّلْغَيْبِ in this rare branch means a depression in the ground that hides what enters it; ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ means places where the side lies against the ground, making a shared low-place image.

after: Fear takes the form of a danger concealed inside a dense grove. The hidden thicket gives spatial shape to apprehension of what may be coming.
reason: لِّلْغَيْبِ here is a thick grove in which things disappear; تَخَافُونَ means anticipating something harmful, so the pair pictures fear of what remains concealed.

after: The absent person’s reputation can either be guarded or exposed to harmful talk. The rare sense of backbiting makes the guarding word answer directly to speech behind someone’s back.
reason: لِّلْغَيْبِ in this branch means speaking ill of a person in their absence; حَٰفِظَٰتٌ means preserving and guarding, so the senses oppose damaging and protecting what is absent.

after: The thin covering over the entrails can faintly picture what guardianship keeps enclosed.
reason: لِّلْغَيْبِ here is the fine fat covering a sheep’s intestines; حَٰفِظَٰتٌ means guarding, so a bodily covering offers a limited image of protection.

after: A hidden root system can be imagined as the concealed source from which expenditure flows outward.
reason: لِّلْغَيْبِ in this branch means roots hidden under the earth; أَنفَقُوا۟ means causing resources to go out, making a faint source-and-outflow image.

after: What is spent leaves the holder’s field of possession, like something hidden away beneath the earth. The expenditure ground therefore carries a faint image of disappearance.
reason: لِّلْغَيْبِ here means burying a dead person in a grave; أَنفَقُوا۟ means spending or causing wealth to go out, so both can be heard through loss from view.

after: Burial pulls downward into concealment, while nushūz rises upward into view. The opposing directions sharpen the feared state as an emergence from its proper place.
reason: لِّلْغَيْبِ in this rare branch means putting the dead into a grave; نُشُوزَهُنَّ in the supplied sense is elevation or protrusion, a clear downward-versus-upward contrast.

after: Bodily qiyām has its footing in the limb named by ٱلرِّجَالُ in the supplied sense. The role of standing over others is shaded by the literal body that stands on a leg.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means standing upright with the body; ٱلرِّجَالُ is glossed here as the leg, the supporting part of that posture.

after: Bodily standing can be one enacted posture of devotional obedience.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means erect bodily standing, while قَٰنِتَٰتٌ means religious obedience; the link is a general one between a worship posture and devotion.

after: The bodily sense of qiyām meets the rising image in nushūz. The feared relational state thus carries a literal upward movement in the same verse as the standing role.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means standing upright; نُشُوزَهُنَّ is glossed as elevation or protrusion, so both words share the movement of rising.

after: The upright body is placed against the body lying on its side. The physical contrast makes the verse’s movement between standing and bed-space vivid.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means erect bodily standing; ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ names places of lying down, the opposite posture.

after: Standing can be imagined as a bodily posture from which a blow is delivered.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means standing upright, and وَٱضْرِبُوهُنَّ means striking; standing is a possible posture for the action, though not required by its plain sense.

after: The root’s bodily standing lends a concrete vertical axis to the human role. عَلِيًّا turns that axis toward God’s exalted height, placing bodily uprightness beside transcendence.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means an erect body, while عَلِيًّا means high or exalted; their shared vertical image moves from bodily posture to divine height.

after: Resolving to undertake a task is imagined as rising to it. Beside نُشُوزَهُنَّ, the same upward motion becomes relational rather than purposeful.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means resolve and rising to an affair; نُشُوزَهُنَّ means a physical rise or protrusion, so one image links determination with bodily rising.

after: Determinedly rising to a task is set against the bed’s lying-down posture. The pair makes the shift from resolve to rest unmistakable.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means resolve and rising to undertake something; ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ are places for lying down, contrasting purposeful rising with repose.

after: Governance and obedience can be heard as paired roles in the verse’s household profile.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means care and governance; قَٰنِتَٰتٌ means religious obedience, making a broad governor-and-obedient pairing.

after: The care named by qiwāma is repeated in the guardians’ keeping. The two words describe sustained responsibility from the governing side and the preserving side.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means managing, caring for, and guarding; حَٰفِظَٰتٌ means guardians or preservers, so the meanings converge on stewardship.

after: The governing sense of qiwāma is echoed in the direct act of divine preservation. Care is heard both as an ongoing charge and as an act of keeping safe.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means care and preservation; حَفِظَ means to guard or preserve, giving the two words a shared sense.

after: The striking command may be heard as one possible enforcement act within a governance sense.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means care, guardianship, and management; وَٱضْرِبُوهُنَّ means striking, a possible but thinly connected exercise of authority.

after: The role of governance meets its counterpart in compliance. The conditional restraint that follows then limits what that authority may pursue.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means governing and managing; أَطَعْنَكُمْ means that they complied, completing a clear authority-and-response relation.

after: Human stewardship is placed beneath the divine predicate of exaltedness. The coda makes qiwāma sound like a limited responsibility under a higher authority.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means exercising care and guardianship, whereas عَلِيًّا names God as exalted; the pair sets human responsibility beneath divine height.

after: The sense of occupying or keeping a place is set against rising out of place. The contrast turns nushūz into a movement away from settled position.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch evokes a place where one stays or stands; نُشُوزَهُنَّ means rising or protruding, so settled station and rising away pull in opposite directions.

after: The standing-place or station is placed beside the beds, where bodies lie down. The verse’s space is marked by opposed postures: standing and reclining.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here carries the sense of a place of standing or residence; ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ means lying-down places, contrasting the two bodily settings.

after: A place of remaining lightly echoes the verb of being or presence.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch can mean a settled place, while كَانَ marks being or occurrence; both touch on presence, but only broadly.

after: The rare sense of qiwāma is equilibrium, while فَضَّلَ carries increase and surplus. Their pairing makes the allocated excess answer to a demand for balance.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means straightness, moderation, and equilibrium; فَضَّلَ means increase or what remains beyond, making balance and excess opposites.

after: Rectitude in qiwāma meets soundness in the women’s profile. The first names upright measure, and the second names what is fit and free of corruption.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means uprightness and evenness; فَٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ means goodness and soundness, so both name rectitude.

after: The steady, straight course is heard in the women’s obedience. Devotion becomes a form of remaining on the right line.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means uprightness and steadiness on a course; قَٰنِتَٰتٌ means devoted obedience, matching the branch’s sense of adherence to obedience.

after: A path that stays clear and unbroken faintly echoes the work of guardianship.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch evokes a straight, unbroken way; حَٰفِظَٰتٌ means preserving or guarding, so both carry a general idea of keeping things on course.

after: The level course is set against a protrusion that rises out of it. This geometric contrast gives the feared nushūz a visible deviation from evenness.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means balance, straightness, and an even course; نُشُوزَهُنَّ means elevation or protrusion, which interrupts that level line.

after: A blow can faintly suggest a disturbance of the balance named by the rare branch.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means equilibrium and evenness; وَٱضْرِبُوهُنَّ means striking, which can unsettle balance, though that effect is not inherent in the verb.

after: Upright adherence is heard again in the act of compliance. The rare branch makes obedience sound like remaining on a straight course.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means staying upright on a steady course; أَطَعْنَكُمْ means complying and following, so both express adherence.

after: The straight and even course meets the word for a path. The closing prohibition is heard as guarding against a departure from the proper way.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means rectitude and a level course; سَبِيلًا means an extended path, so the senses share the image of a way to follow.

after: Uprightness and divine height share a vertical image, though one is measure and the other exaltedness.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means straightness and uprightness; عَلِيًّا means high or exalted, so the verticality is an image rather than a full synonym.

after: What exceeds a share can become the material that sustains a household.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means a support or livelihood foundation; فَضَّلَ means increase or surplus, which can supply that foundation in a general way.

after: The wealth named in the verse becomes the material basis of maintenance. The rare support sense turns the spending ground into what holds livelihood up.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means a pillar or basis of livelihood; أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ names their wealth, which supplies a concrete part of that support.

after: Valuation and greatness can meet on a scale of magnitude.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means a price or assessed value; كَبِيرًا means large or great, so a large measure faintly suggests high value.

after: A person’s stature is built on the legs that bear the body. The rare bodily sense of qiwāma thus gives the limb word a supporting role.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means stature or the body’s height; ٱلرِّجَالُ is glossed in the worklist as the leg, a part that supports bodily stature.

after: The body’s height and the rise of nushūz share a vertical image. What is a measured stature in one word becomes a protrusion or rising in the other.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means bodily height and stature; نُشُوزَهُنَّ means elevation or protrusion, so both meet in vertical extension.

after: A well-formed upright body is set against the places where bodies lie down. The bed-space makes the posture of stature more sharply felt.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means a person’s upright stature; ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ means lying-down places, opposing upright form and reclining posture.

after: Bodily height resonates with the predicate of divine height. The shared vertical dimension moves from human stature to exaltedness.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means bodily height or stature; عَلِيًّا means high and exalted, so the two senses meet in height.

after: Stature and greatness overlap as dimensions of bodily size.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means stature and height; كَبِيرًا means great or large, giving a broad size relation rather than a precise synonym.

after: The rare branch includes a standing leg or support as part of an apparatus. The leg word thus meets qiwāma in the concrete part that bears a structure.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here evokes an upright or supporting component of a device; ٱلرِّجَالُ is glossed as the leg, a bodily support with the same structural role.

after: A component of an apparatus faintly echoes a portion of a larger group.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch can name a structural part or tool; بَعْضَهُمْ means some or a portion of them, making a general part-whole link.

after: The apparatus-part sense can be lightly heard beside the comparison’s unnamed portion.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here evokes a supporting component of a device, while بَعْضٍ means a part or portion; their overlap is partitive but generic.

after: A striking action may involve a supporting tool or a held part that transmits force. That apparatus image gives the command’s physical impact a concrete mechanism.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means a standing component or held tool-part; وَٱضْرِبُوهُنَّ means striking one thing against another, an action that can involve such an instrument.

after: A raised component offers a small structural echo of exalted height.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here includes a raised or upright part of a device; عَلِيًّا means high or exalted, linking a physical high point with the divine predicate.

after: The image of people standing at resurrection lightly calls on the legs that support them.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means the Day of Resurrection and the standing of creatures; ٱلرِّجَالُ is glossed here as a leg, a bodily part involved in standing.

after: The resurrection image places the raised creatures before the deity they worship.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here evokes the day when creation stands for judgment; ٱللَّهُ names the worshipped being, a broad relation between resurrection and its divine judge.

after: Devotional obedience belongs naturally to the religious horizon of resurrection.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means the day of rising for judgment; قَٰنِتَٰتٌ means religious obedience, a general link between devotion and the judgment day.

after: The one who guards is also heard, in a broad theological sense, as the one before whom people rise.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here carries the resurrection-day sense; ٱللَّهُ is the deity named as guarding in the verse, so the relation is a general one between divine care and divine judgment.

after: The final divine name gathers the verse toward the one before whom creation will stand. The resurrection sense makes the closing greatness sound like the authority of the judge.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means the day when creatures rise before God; ٱللَّهَ names God in the closing assertion, completing the relation between standing for judgment and the divine judge.

after: The event of rising and the verb of being both touch on occurrence.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means the occurrence of resurrection; كَانَ marks being or occurrence in time, a real but broad link.

after: The rare combat sense meets the physical act of striking as one of its concrete actions. The confrontation image becomes immediate rather than abstract resistance.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means resisting or fighting an opponent; وَٱضْرِبُوهُنَّ means striking, a concrete act within a contest.

after: A fixed, equal weight is set against surplus and increase. The balance image makes the allocation language sound as though measured equality is being tested by excess.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means money of equal weight that does not tip the balance; فَضَّلَ means increase or surplus, making equal measure and excess opposites.

after: The stillness associated with devotional practice can faintly accompany obedient devotion.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means stopping or becoming still; قَٰنِتَٰتٌ means religious obedience, so the link is a general image of composed worship.

after: An animal halted by exhaustion faintly contrasts with the movement away implied by separation.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ here means stopping or being unable to continue; وَٱهْجُرُوهُنَّ means breaking a bond and departing, a thin contrast between stoppage and separation.

after: The sun at its zenith faintly evokes the shadow falling close to a person’s feet.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means the sun at midday overhead; ٱلرِّجَالُ is glossed as the leg, making a tentative image of the sun’s vertical axis meeting the feet.

after: The zenith is when the sun stands at the day’s center, while the unseen remains beyond sight. Their juxtaposition sets full exposure against concealment at the moment of greatest visibility.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch means the midday sun overhead; لِّلْغَيْبِ means what is hidden from sight, giving visible zenith and concealment a clear opposition.

after: The day’s solar apex can faintly echo the magnitude named by greatness.
reason: قَوَّٰمُونَ in this branch evokes the sun at its highest point; كَبِيرًا means great or large, so the relation is an image of peak and magnitude.
